exclusions.A: It struck Abel, running his thumb along it, that Rusk had known from the start how this would end.
exclusions.C: Abel looked for a broken string, ready to fit a new one, and found every string sound.
exclusions.D: He tuned it anyway, note by note, at Rusk's pitch, for one more evening.
exclusions.E: The piano stood where it always had, at the far end from the stove.

WV10-P01.4.note: The realisation came to Abel ('it struck Abel ... that Rusk had known'), so the sense is 'dawned on', not a physical blow or a deliberate conclusion.

exclusions.A: Abel kept his hand on the lid.
exclusions.C: That's gone now, and tuning won't fetch it back.
exclusions.E: He pressed the low C once and listened to it fade.

WV10-P01.5.note: He reassures Nell about Saturday, then fondly recalls how the bass 'rang like a bell' twenty years ago and accepts it is gone: wistful.

exclusions.A: The dispute ran through eleven meetings and two winters, until a councillor raised the matter of the common's drains and the yard won by one vote.
exclusions.B: Nora wanted it on the common; the council wanted the station yard.
exclusions.D: Where the carousel would stand was another matter.
exclusions.E: By then the raffle, its tickets printed with a photograph taken in 1923 of the carousel in full swing, had sold out in a week and paid for the restoration.

WV10-P02.4.note: A councillor 'raised the matter' in a meeting, i.e. brought it up or mentioned it.

exclusions.A: He hitched up the trailer that afternoon.
exclusions.C: Hal and Nora had sung side by side in the chapel choir for twenty years.
exclusions.D: When she asked for the grey, he told her she could have it if she could catch it, and led her to a stall where the wooden horse stood between his two real ones, wearing a halter, a bucket of oats at its feet.
exclusions.E: He hitched up the trailer that afternoon.

WV10-P02.5.note: Telling her she can have the wooden horse 'if she could catch it' and stabling it with a halter and oats is a joke, and he gives it up the same afternoon: playful.

exclusions.B: Over the winter the park had put up a sand fence that ran the whole length of the dune foot, its slats a hand's width apart.
exclusions.C: Much had changed on the spit that year.
exclusions.D: Every July Vell sets forty pitfall traps along the dune crest.
exclusions.E: A March storm tore away the dune's seaward face and much of the old crest with it.

WV10-P03.4.note: A fence that 'ran the whole length of the dune foot' stretched or extended along it.

exclusions.A: Vell moved the traps up onto the new crest.
exclusions.C: She had crossed out her own name on its first page and written his above it.
exclusions.D: Vell said he would be the one to tell them, and slid the season report across the desk.
exclusions.E: This July the count was seven hundred and eighty; last year's figure, she now writes, measured the traps rather than the beetles.

WV10-P03.5.note: Giving Arkin the credit, even putting his name above hers on the report, shows she admires his discovery.
